trials.name: CTC vocabulary boosting on Ultra
trials.summary: synthetic term hits up to 99% from 78%, dictation WER up to 8.18% from 4.67%, p95 3.1× slower
trials.role: Speech recognition, custom words (dictation and meetings)
trials.model: FluidAudio CTC vocabulary boosting (parakeet-ctc-110m, `VocabularyBoostingSession.rescore`) on Parakeet Ultra, with and without CustomWordMatcher
trials.against: Ultra + CustomWordMatcher (the app; meetings apply no custom words)
trials.hypothesis: Boosting raises custom-word accuracy without other-word WER rising over 0.2 points; risk is speed (~3.4× slower earlier, which would put Ultra's 97 ms p95 over 300 ms)
trials.metric: 15 custom words (10 with aliases); 50 real dictations (2 carry a custom word), 12 meeting tracks (2 carry one), 90 synthesised `say` term sentences; hit rate, WER, false insertions, p50/p95, N× realtime
trials.result: Synth hits 53% plain, 78% A, 99% boosted, 100% boosted + matcher. Dictation WER 4.67% A vs 8.18% boosted, p50/p95 51/117 ms A vs 169/359 ms boosted (3.3×/3.1× slower), 26 false insertions vs 5. Meetings WER 15.22% A vs 18.57% boosted, 227× vs 58× realtime. Needs a second model, 101 MB
trials.held: speed yes (3.1× slower, over the 300 ms p95); custom-word gain yes on synthetic speech; other-word WER no

trials.name: Custom-word matcher retuned for Ultra
trials.summary: 0 false insertions and dictation WER 4.09%, same as plain Ultra; 71% of synthetic term hits
trials.model: CustomWordMatcher retuned for Parakeet Ultra: dictionary words are not replaced on sound alone, a confident word does not join an unsure one in a run, +0.05 sound bar per extra word
trials.against: CustomWordMatcher as tuned on transcribe.cpp confidences
trials.hypothesis: Retuned thresholds bring false insertions to about 0 and real-dictation WER to within 0.2 points of plain Ultra (4.29% or less) while keeping 70% or more of synthetic term hits
trials.metric: 15 custom words (10 with aliases); 50 real dictations (2 carry one), 12 meeting tracks, 90 synthesised `say` term sentences; clips split by hash parity into tune and held-out halves, sweep on tune, report on held-out; WER, hits, false insertions
trials.result: Thresholds alone could not do it: the 5 real and 1 synthetic false insertions were all unsure words (confidence 0.5 to 0.68) with sound keys equal or one edit away, and the correct words Ultra scores that low (5% under 0.75, 34 of 669) look the same, so no confidence or similarity setting separated them. Three structural rules did: 2 of the 5 were dictionary words, 3 were a confident word carried into a term by an unsure neighbour (2 words each), and the run penalty cut multi-word meeting false matches 31 to 14. After: dictation WER 4.09% (plain Ultra 4.09%, was 4.67%), 0 false insertions real and synthetic, synthetic hits 64/90 (71%, was 70/90), real hits 0/2 (unchanged). Held-out: WER 3.57% both, 0 false, synthetic 35/49 (71%). Meetings: 14 false matches over 16,674 words against 2 for plain Ultra (99 before); 10 of the 14 come from stored aliases, and with aliases off it is 6. Matcher with dictionary check p95 1.2 ms
trials.held: yes: false insertions 0, WER 4.09% (within 0.2), synthetic hits 71%; meetings not safe while aliases apply

trials.hypothesis: Meetings 0.3–1.0 points better than Ultra (claimed AMI-Cleaned 7.16 against v3's 9.42; same architecture, English fine-tune at full precision), dictation a tie. Predicted p95 150–200 ms, 1.3–1.6 GB resident (risk to the 1.5 GB dictation budget), Neural Engine, 1.23 GB file (2× Ultra). Wrong if meetings are not more than 0.2 points better, or dictation is more than 0.2 points worse
trials.metric: WER vs AssemblyAI Universal-3.5 Pro, unprompted (`ASSEMBLYAI_PROMPT=''`; the verbatim-prompted references are not built), 50 dictations and 12 meeting tracks, 24 spans hand-checked, with and without fillers; S/D/I per track; p50/p95; peak memory; CPU and GPU %
trials.result: Dictation 4.17% vs 4.32% (29 vs 30 errors); fillers dropped 4.22% vs 4.22%. Meetings 14.11% vs 13.20%; fillers dropped 13.12% vs 12.65% (+0.47). 508 deletions vs 230, worse on 8 of 12 tracks; on one 24 s room clip it writes 27 of about 70 words, leaving out quieter background speech, and the first 14 s alone lose the same words, so it is the model, not chunking. Fewer insertions (717 vs 980), which the listen review found are mostly real speech for Ultra. Dictation p50/p95 59/125 ms vs 57/131 ms, same session. Peak resident 1,094 MiB on the first run, while the Neural Engine compiled the encoder, vs 643 MiB for Ultra's; 146 vs 120 MiB once compiled. The first compile took 99 min; later loads 0.3 s. Meetings 142× vs 240× realtime. CPU 104% vs 123% mean, GPU 22% vs 7% mean (Neural Engine for both). Not a quiet Mac: Spotlight indexing at ~340% CPU, another session's script at 100%, GPU baseline 25–67%

trials.name: FluidAudio 0.17.6 speaker embeddings
trials.summary: wrong-speaker words 1,691 vs 1,700 of 182,436 (0.93% both); the 9 that changed were checked by ear
trials.model: FluidAudio 0.17.6: digitally silent frames left out of the FBank mean (#988); `embedSpan` tiles short spans (#982), a path the app never takes (zero-vote re-embed is off)
trials.hypothesis: Written first: no more words under the wrong speaker, fewer where a short speaker is folded into the nearest voice; Nemotron's turns unchanged. Wrong if the rate rises over 0.2 points or the right number of people falls
trials.metric: Words under the wrong speaker against AssemblyAI Universal-3.5 Pro labels, through `nemotron_app` (Nemotron turns, one WeSpeaker embedding per speaker, `SpeakerMerge.absorbingShort`), 71 meeting tracks; right number of people
trials.result: 1,691 vs 1,700 of 182,436 words (0.93% both); right number of people on 53 of 71 for both. Turns identical on all 71 tracks; one track's merge changed (6.1 s of talk, 9 fewer wrong words). Diff has no speech-model source changes. The 9 words are two stretches 0.17.5 gave one voice and 0.17.6 and AssemblyAI another; heard against a sample of each voice on 24 October, both were 0.17.6's
trials.held: yes, by a small margin, and the change checked by ear

trials.name: Tiled voice-name clips
trials.summary: short clips named right 2,990 vs 1,183 of 3,306; strangers reaching 0.5 rose from 2 to 18, so the cut moved to 0.8
trials.model: Voice-name clips tiled to fill the WeSpeaker window, every frame weighted (FluidAudio #982's recipe), in `Diarizer.voice(of:)`
trials.against: Clips zero-padded, weights over the frames they cover
trials.hypothesis: Written first: as many right names (76 of 77 on 6 October) with no more strangers at 0.5, and the gain on clips under ~4 s. Wrong if right names fall or a stranger reaches 0.5 that did not before
trials.metric: Each call named from the others (64 calls, 26 people, 306 voices), then each voice's person removed as a stranger (326); the app's gradient descent; single clips under 4 s; suggestions at posterior cuts 0.5 to 0.9
trials.result: Voices right 302 vs 300; single clips under 4 s right 2,990 vs 1,183 of 3,306. Strangers at 0.5: 18 vs 2. At 0.8, tiled suggests 291 right names, 2 wrong, 2 strangers; padded at 0.5 suggests 278, 2, 2. Padded and tiled embeddings of one clip under 6 s are unrelated (median cosine 0.0 to 0.16)
trials.held: partly: right names yes, strangers at 0.5 no
trials.verdict: shipped with the cut at 0.8; voice files learned padded are relearned
